source.title: Zatom-1: Towards a Multimodal Foundation Model for 3D Molecules and Materials
source.authors: Alex Morehead; M. Cretu; Antonia Panescu; Rishabh Anand; Maurice Weiler; Tynan Perez; Samuel M. Blau; Steven Farrell; W. Bhimji; Anubhav Jain; Hrushikesh P. Sahasrabuddhe; Pietro Liò; T. Jaakkola; Rafael Gómez-Bombarelli; Rex Ying; N. Erichson; Michael W. Mahoney

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: Reports a model-size sweep for 3D molecule/material generation, a new setting, but does not test whether the specified language-model loss laws or compute-optimal allocation hold.
record.gate_note: Figure 3 reports training loss and generation validity trends across model sizes, with correlations at epoch 2,000. These are relevant to scaling but are not held-out language-model cross-entropy, fitted power laws, or a compute-optimal allocation result. Other benchmark results are not scaling-law findings and are omitted.
record.test_reason: The scaling evidence is a three-point sweep (80M, 160M, 300M; under half an order of magnitude) of a 3D chemical flow-matching model. It reports Pearson/Spearman correlations of training loss and validity with size at epoch 2,000. There is no power-law fit, no held-out loss, no extrapolation, no compute-optimal sweep and no shape ablation at fixed parameters. Training loss falling with size cannot show the power-law form V5 names, so no version is tested. The paper invokes neural scaling (citing Kaplan) to claim 'predictable gains' but does not test the law.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors state that training and validation metrics 'improve predictably' with model size (Figure 3, Pearson r > 0.96), suggesting scaling potential. They defer parallel data and model scaling (e.g., OMol25 100M) to future work because of compute limits. Note that Figure 3 shows training loss and validity rates, not validation loss.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales a multimodal 3D chemical generative model and reports training-loss and generation-validity trends; it does not reproduce language-model held-out-loss scaling-law fits or compute-optimal allocation methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Model size changes the reported training-loss and generation-validity trends across 80M, 160M, and 300M models.

fits_no_version.finding: At epoch 2,000, training loss decreases monotonically with size across 80M/160M/300M (Pearson=-1.00, Spearman=-1.00).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a 3D chemical flow-matching Transformer, training loss decreases monotonically with parameter count over a ~4x range. No power-law form is established.

fits_no_version.finding: Molecule validity (Pearson 0.97) and crystal validity (Pearson 0.99) rise with size at epoch 2,000. Benchmark results, however, are non-monotonic: QM9 validity 95.26 (160M) vs 95.19 (300M), and LeMat MSUN 0.64 (160M) vs 0.36 (300M).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sample-quality metrics of chemical generative models do not necessarily improve monotonically with model size even when training loss does.

record.problems: The scaling evidence covers only three model sizes and reports correlations rather than fitted scaling laws; the training-loss result is not held-out loss. The authors note resource constraints on larger model and data scaling experiments.
record.rows_left_out: No other scaling-related results were reported separately in a way that adds a distinct model-size trend; other generation and prediction benchmarks do not test the claim versions.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss and no power-law fit over orders of magnitude.
No small-run fits used to predict larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation of parameters versus data.
Depth is fixed at 16 blocks; width varies only together with parameter count, so there is no shape-at-fixed-size comparison.
No power-law form is fitted for this modality (3D molecules/materials); only monotonic trends over 3 sizes.
Downstream property prediction is reported only for the 80M model; there is no scale dependence.
No fitted exponents or fitting-choice sensitivity.

missing.what: Crystal validity vs size correlation at epoch 2,000 (Pearson=0.99, Spearman=1.00)
Final benchmark metrics across the 80M/160M/300M sweep showing non-monotonic gains (e.g., Metastable% 51.8/71.5/64.3; MSUN 0.36/0.64/0.36; QM9 validity 94.94/95.26/95.19)

record.verdict_notes: The record's relation 'tests' with every version marked not_tested is internally inconsistent, so it is reclassified as discusses/T6. The size sweep confounds parameters with learning rate, gradient accumulation and training time (Table 5). The paper is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or power-law fits in parameters, tokens, or compute are reported.
No small-run fits or predictions of much larger runs are reported.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token scaling is reported.
The architecture comparison in Appendix E does not hold parameter count fixed while varying depth or width.
The study uses chemical data and reports size-related trends, but does not test whether the same power-law form holds across modalities or training regimes.
Downstream prediction results are reported, but not their predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
No fitted scaling exponents, compute-optimal splits, or sensitivity of such fits to setup choices are reported.

rows.subject: Z ATOM -1 size sweep (80M, 160M, 300M)
rows.operation_detail: Compared training loss across model sizes during training; reports the parameter-size correlation at epoch 2,000.
rows.note: The paper reports correlations across the three model sizes; this is training loss for a chemical generative model, not held-out language-model cross-entropy or a fitted power law.
rows.check: Training (not held-out) flow-matching loss at three sizes. A rank/linear correlation over 3 points within about 4x in parameters cannot show a power law, so it does not bear on V1 or V5. The sizes also differ in learning rate (1e-3, 5e-4, 2.5e-4), batch/accumulation and training hours (24h, 48h, 96h), confounding size with schedule.

rows.subject: Z ATOM -1 size sweep (80M, 160M, 300M)
rows.operation_detail: Compared generation validity across model sizes; reports the parameter-size correlation at epoch 2,000.
rows.note: The paper reports correlations across the three model sizes; validity is not a loss measure.
rows.check: Mislabelled. Pearson=0.97/Spearman=1.00 is the molecule (QM9) validity panel of Figure 3, not generic 'generation validity'. The crystal validity panel (Pearson=0.99, Spearman=1.00) is not recorded. Validity is a sample-quality rate, not loss, and no scaling form is fitted.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
